parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by nuclear fusion and nuclear fission.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A nuclear reaction which may, in the future, be used for the generation of electrical energy is

$${}^{2}_{1}\text{H} + {}^{3}_{1}\text{H} \rightarrow {}^{4}_{2}\text{He} + x.$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.stem:
Data for the binding energy per nucleon $E_{B}$ of some nuclei are given in Fig. 12.1.

| {{blank}} | binding energy per nucleon $E_B\,/\,10^{-13}\,\mathrm{J}$ |
| --- | --- |
| deuterium $^{2}_{1}\mathrm{H}$ | 1.7813 |
| tritium $^{3}_{1}\mathrm{H}$ | 4.5285 |
| helium $^{4}_{2}\mathrm{He}$ | 11.3290 |

Fig. 12.1
parts.text:
1. State the binding energy per nucleon of $x$.

2. Calculate the energy change that takes place in this reaction.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (ii) part 2 to determine the energy release when $2.0\text{ g}$ of deuterium (${}^{2}_{1}\text{H}$) reacts with $3.0\text{ g}$ of tritium (${}^{3}_{1}\text{H}$).
